title: CARE OF MEDICAL EQUIPMENT
knowledge: Identifies medical equipment care which adheres to infection control standards of patient's safety.
skills: Upon disinfecting of equipment's (e.g. vital signs machine, incubators and radiant warmers), all detachable parts must be removed and scrubbed in the utility room.
Unused medical equipment should be thoroughly cleaned and dried up in the reservoir for 24 hours after disinfection.
Upon cleaning an occupied incubator, patient must be transferred temporarily to a radiant warmer then to be put back after cleaning of incubator is done.
Ensures that PPM is updated for all the machines and equipment.
Checklist readily available.

title: CODE RED
knowledge: Describe activation of Code Red.
Discuss RACE.
Explain PASS.
Describe how to evacuate horizontally and vertically in area of practice.
Discuss how to evacuate patient who is bed bound for any reason including those who are vulnerable and/ or have special needs.
Discuss the rational for a reflection session in and on practice after a Code Red and how to activate findings to improve future practice and response.
skills: Demonstrate the role of the Safety Coordinator in area of practice.
Show the evaluator of the placement of the Safety Coordinator jacket/ tag/ lanyard relevant to area of practice.
Demonstrate activation of Code Red.
Demonstrate how to apply Pass.
Demonstrate how to evacuate a patient who is bed bound for any reason including those who are vulnerable and/ or have special needs.
Show the evaluator the placement of the evacuation plan, various fire extinguisher and hoses and exits in area of practice.
Complete the checking and documentation of a fire extinguisher and explain why this is necessary and how often this procedure is required.
Demonstrate how to organize and facilitate a reflection session in and on practice a Code Red.
attitude: Ability of Nurse to respond professionally and calmly in a Code Red situation.
Ability to facilitate activation, response and evacuation in Code Red.
Ability of Nurse to acknowledge limitations in knowledge and skills in Code Red situation.
Ability to communicate with Fire Chief and respond to instruction as relevant and appropriate.
Demonstrate ability to organize and facilitate a reflection session in and on practice after a Code Red and activate findings to improve future practice and response.

title: DISASTER PREPAREDNESS
knowledge: Describe the difference between Internal and External Disaster.
Verbalizes actions to be taken in potential or declared Disasters affecting the organizations operations.
Differentiate actions to be taken in External and Internal Disasters.
Differentiate between Alert, Partial and Full Response Modes, verbalizes actions appropriate to each mode.
Verbalize understanding of Disaster Plan Activation protocols and Chain of Command.
Identify location and objectives of facility specific control centers.
Verbalize understanding of actions undertaken by other units/ department which specifically impact area of practice during Disaster.
Describe actions undertaken by all staff during a Disaster – including appropriate personal role.
Describe Disaster triage and main receiving areas – other units as appropriate to area of practice.
Describe how to register and document during a Disaster for both disaster victims and routine patients.
Verbalizes knowledge of staffing contingency plans/ call – out procedures during disaster situations.
Differentiate actions to be taken out-of-hours and during regular hours when other key personnel are present.
Verbalize actions to be taken to activate transport services for staff during a disaster.
Discuss rationale and importance for post disaster critique.
skills: Demonstrate ability to activate Internal Disaster in the area of practice.
Complete the registration and document of both Disaster victims and routine patients during a disaster.
Demonstrate the activation of staffing contingency plans / call-out procedures during disaster situations.
Complete the actions to be taken out-of-hours and during regular hours when other key personnel are present.
Participate in: in-service training, disaster drills, disaster critiques.
Demonstrate ability to perform disaster role appropriate to usual position and back-up role (e.g. CN to know Head Nurse's role).
Demonstrate means of communication during a disaster.
Shows how to complete deactivation process when disaster called as "All Clear and Stand Down" and how to facilitate a debriefing session for staff.
Participates in a Disaster critique.
attitude: Ability of Nurse to respond professionally and calmly in a disaster situation.
Ability to facilitate activation and response in a disaster situation.
Ability of Nurse to acknowledge limitations in knowledge and skills in a disaster situation.
Ability to communicate with key personnel and response to instruction as relevant and appropriate.
Demonstrate ability to organize and facilitate a reflection session in and on practice after a disaster situation and activate findings to improve practice and response.
